title: Compute brief - 5 November 2026
description: The market priced the election: the Philadelphia chip index fell 8% and CoreWeave and Nebius lost 11% and 15% as analysts put roughly half the US hyperscale pipeline at regulatory risk. Texas's governor-elect says the pause stays until new laws pass, and OpenAI published a Compute Campus Policy. Wire: Lambda's $33.1 billion Alabama campus, Microsoft passes on more Nscale Texas capacity, PDG finances Johor, IndiaAI opens a 10,000-GPU round. Tape: 70 confirms, 0 ticks, 0 NEW.
og_kicker: The chips are sold. The sites are now on the ballot.
lede: Two days after US voters backed data center restrictions in 40 of 41 local ballot measures, the market repriced the build: Reuters reported the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 8% on Thursday, with CoreWeave down 11% and Nebius 15%. Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa said she will keep the state's pause in place until the legislature passes local votes, no-NDA rules and ratepayer protections; BMI says 53% of hyperscaler pipeline growth sits in newly flipped governor states, and Cleanview counts 159 GW, or 41% of planned US capacity, where new governors back a pause. Builders are answering with terms: OpenAI pledged to drop NDAs and pay its full power cost, and Lambda named itself anchor of a $33.1 billion, 1 GW campus in Alabama while promising the same. Live list prices did not move: 70 confirms, 0 ticks and 0 NEW, with Lambda H100 at $3.99 and Crusoe's 1 December rates still scheduled, not live.
